findings.where: electron/lib/autonomyGate.cjs — normalise() and namesGovernedPath(); consumed by inspectCreate (both origins) and by upgradeApplier.applyWith step 3
findings.problem: normalise() only converts backslashes, strips a leading './' and lowercases — it never resolves path structure. namesGovernedPath() then compares against the four repo-relative SELF_GOVERNING_PATHS with === and endsWith('/'+rel), so 'electron/lib/./autonomyStop.cjs', 'electron//lib/autonomyStop.cjs' and 'electron/lib/../lib/autonomyStop.cjs' all return null. Confirmed end to end: a self-upgrade proposal with meta.schema set, a tier-0 user and one patch change naming 'electron/lib/./autonomyStop.cjs' with a correct baseSha256 was applied by applyWith against a fixture repo with no refusal, and the stop module on disk afterwards read 'function isStopped(){return false;}'. The same string inside meta passes fileProposal's scan, and the renderer create fence returns no refusal either — autonomyStop.cjs is not in loyaltyGuard.PROTECTED_FILES, so nothing downstream objects and timeline.cjs's SELF_MODIFY applier writes changes[].path verbatim. Both halves of the narrowed FR-14 claim in docs/research/self-upgrade-build.md §2 ('unreachable by this design's applier and by the renderer create path') are therefore false. I6 still holds — a recorded master approval is required — but the diff should not have been fileable.
findings.fix: Canonicalise by resolution before comparing, the way the pre-existing loyaltyGuard already does (it correctly refuses 'electron/lib/./loyaltyGuard.cjs' and 'electron/lib/../lib/loyaltyGuard.cjs' on the same input): in normalise(), after the separator swap, run the result through path.posix.normalize (or resolve against the repo root and take the relative path) before lowercasing, and keep the basename matching for the out-of-repo stop state. Then add suite rows in scripts/verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs asserting that the './', '//' and '..' variants of each of the four SELF_GOVERNING_PATHS are refused at inspectCreate for both origins and at applyWith, so the hole cannot reopen.

findings.where: electron/lib/autonomyPolicy.cjs — FLOORS/CEILINGS for 'revert-own-apply' and validate(); electron/lib/upgradeApplier.cjs — the policy.requireMasterDriven('revert-own-apply','L4') entry gate
findings.problem: 'revert-own-apply' is not in PERMANENT, so the data file may lower it. With shared/autonomy-policy.json present and {"version":1,"levels":{"revert-own-apply":"L0"}} the file validates clean (source=file, rejected=false) and requireMasterDriven then returns a refusal, so applyWith throws 'autonomy policy: "revert-own-apply" is L0 (forbidden); L4 (apply-after-approval) required for a master-driven act' — confirmed by running it against the live loader. A master-approved apply is refused again, which is the defect class the first assertions of verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs exist to catch, now reachable through a documented, validator-accepted edit. It is also not what the module says the edit does: autonomyPolicy.cjs's header claims a present file is 'how master ... turns the automatic revert off' and that 'setting revert-own-apply to L0 in the data file still genuinely disables the automatic revert', but revert() consults neither the policy nor the stop, so the automatic revert keeps running while the apply is blocked. Compounding it: current() caches the first load for the process lifetime and reload() has no production caller, so deleting the file does not restore applies until a restart. No suite row covers a present data file, and §4 of the build note concedes the live load() path has only ever taken its absent branch.
findings.fix: Resolve MASTER_ACT classes at the applier's entry gate against the frozen FLOORS rather than the data-file-intersected level (or move 'revert-own-apply' into PERMANENT so the file is not read for it), and make revert() itself the thing that consults the class if master is to be able to disable the automatic revert. Correct the two sentences in autonomyPolicy.cjs's header to describe what the edit actually does, and add suite rows in scripts/verifyAutonomyStop.cjs and scripts/verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs that write a real shared/autonomy-policy.json lowering 'revert-own-apply' to L0 and assert a master-approved apply still SUCCEEDS.

findings.problem: lift() is the only writer of 'allowed: true' — the single act that enables autonomy — and its success path has no behavioural coverage. It requires './capability.cjs' inline with no injection seam, and 'system.suspend-autonomy' is absent from shared/capabilities.json, so capability.deny refuses every tier including master and the function cannot succeed on any machine. The empty-note refusal, the contents of the allow-file it writes, the write-then-unlink ordering and the halt clearing are therefore asserted only by regex over the source text of the function body. When master adds the capability key, the first real execution of lift() is in production.
findings.fix: Give lift() an injected capability module in the same shape upgradeApplier uses for io (e.g. lift(user, note, { capability } = {}) defaulting to require('./capability.cjs')), then add behavioural rows: a fake capability that grants 'system.suspend-autonomy' must make lift() write a valid allow-file, flip isStopped() to false, clear the stopped-record, and still refuse an empty note.

findings.where: electron/lib/autonomyPolicy.cjs — the reload() doc comment ('Master edits it by hand; no build and no restart is required') and current()
findings.problem: reload() has no production caller anywhere in electron/, and there is no IPC channel for the policy, so current() caches the first load for the process lifetime. A hand edit to shared/autonomy-policy.json does not take effect until the app restarts, which contradicts the comment. The stop itself is unaffected — isStopped() reads the allow-file from disk on every call.
findings.fix: Either drop the 'no restart is required' half of the sentence, or call reload() at the point the policy is consulted for a gating decision (fileProposal and the applier's entry gate) so a hand edit is picked up live.

findings.where: electron/lib/upgradeApplier.cjs — the step-0 comment above the masterDriven check ('a {tier: 0} object is forgeable in-process')
findings.problem: proposals.cjs's 'proposals:apply' handler is ipcMain.handle('proposals:apply', async (_e, id, opts) => apply(id, opts || {})) and apply() authorises opts.user, so the user object the applier reads arrives from the renderer, not only from in-process callers. The hole is pre-existing and lives in a protected file, and the comment is right that masterDriven is insufficient, but 'in-process' understates where the forgery can originate.
findings.fix: Reword the comment to say the user object arrives with the IPC request and is therefore renderer-supplied, and add 'bind proposals:apply's user to the authenticated session rather than the payload' to the 'FOR MASTER' list in docs/research/self-upgrade-build.md §5, since proposals.cjs cannot be edited by this build.

findings.problem: The stop is fail-safe but the create fence is fail-open: if autonomyGate.cjs fails to load, the ledger registers with the bare recorder and the kind fence and path fence vanish for every proposals:create. That is the deliberate I11 degradation, and safeRequire records it in loadFailures, but nothing in the autonomy surface reports it — status() and statusText() would still describe the fence as if it were in place.
findings.fix: Have autonomyStop.status() report whether the gate module loaded (e.g. a gateLoaded field derived by attempting the require) and have statusText() say the create fence is not in place when it is not, so a degraded fence is visible where autonomy is reported rather than only in the boot log.
